📰 U.S. on High Alert: Iranian Drone Attacks Raise Fears of a Wider Middle East War


Tensions between the United States and Iran are rising again after Bahrain reported intercepting several Iranian aerial attacks, raising fears of a wider regional confrontation.

On Sunday, November 15, Bahrain's air defenses intercepted multiple aerial threats following warnings that prompted residents to seek shelter. The country's authorities urged the public to remain calm and follow safety instructions.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for launching six drones toward the U.S. air-defense radar facility at Al-Rifaa, near Riffa Air Base in Bahrain. Tehran described the operation as retaliation for what it called hostile American actions.

However, important details remain disputed. Neither U.S. nor Bahraini authorities immediately confirmed the claimed strike on the facility.

The latest incident followed an earlier Iranian claim involving an American early-warning radar installation. U.S. Central Command said two drones had been intercepted and that the radar facility had not been destroyed.

Bahrain is strategically important to Washington because it hosts the headquarters of the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet. American naval forces based there play a major role in protecting shipping routes and maintaining security across the Persian Gulf and surrounding waters.

The confrontation comes amid stalled diplomatic efforts to end the nearly nine-month U.S.-Israeli war involving Iran, which began on February 28.

Trump has indicated that Washington could avoid further military action if Iran refrains from additional provocations. At the same time, the United States continues to maintain pressure on Tehran.

The biggest concern for regional security experts is the possibility of miscalculation. Even an intercepted drone attack can trigger retaliation, accelerate military escalation and put American personnel and regional allies at risk.

For Washington, the challenge is finding a way to deter further attacks without triggering a much larger conflict.

📄 Ghalibaf: No regional peace without end to Israeli war on Lebanon

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s Parliament speaker has underlined the need for an end to Israel’s war on Lebanon and the restoration of the Arab country's sovereignty over its entire territory as a prerequisite for peace in West Asia.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf made the remarks during a telephone conversation with his Lebanese counterpart, Nabih Berri.
​
“In our view, lasting peace and stability in the region cannot be achieved without an end to the war in Lebanon and the full restoration of Lebanese sovereignty over its entire territory,” he said.
​
He also noted that the Islamic Republic attaches particular importance to the issue of Lebanon in pursuing its demands and conditions in the mediated negotiation process with the United States.
​
He was referring to seven core conditions declared by Iran for renewed talks with the US amid a stalemate in negotiations to permanently end the war. Among those conditions are ending the fighting on all fronts, especially Israel’s attacks on Lebanon.
​
Berri, for his part, called for the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanon in line with UN Security Council Resolution 1701, which ended the 33-day-long Israeli military onslaught on the country in 2006.
​
The Israeli regime keeps attacking Lebanon and occupying areas there in defiance of a truce that took effect on June 20 and a US-brokered framework agreement reached on June 26.
​
The usurping entity has also solidified its occupation of Lebanon’s southern regions, with its officials announcing future settlement plans.
